proposal.observation: Lowering hough_threshold_oblique from the accepted incumbent value of 44 to 40 reduced correspondence_f1@15 by 0.0083 while leaving depth_nan_ratio and ring count unchanged. The before/after depth and segmentation images are effectively stable, but the prompt plot changes the far-right candidate from a midpoint to a negative-slope point and the detected-line view loses useful edge oblique hypotheses, indicating that extra low-vote candidates disrupted line selection rather than fixing an upstream coverage problem.
proposal.rule: Keep the accepted oblique vote threshold and apply ontology remediation r_relax_hough through its alternative control: modestly raise maxLineGap_oblique so fragmented high-support joint evidence can connect without admitting the low-vote candidates rejected in round 2.
proposal.rationale: Round 2 directly shows that further threshold relaxation is harmful, while unchanged depth holes and ring count argue against changing denoising, enhancement, or unfolding. Increasing only maxLineGap_oblique from the accepted incumbent value 47 to 52 stays close to the successful round-1 setting and tests continuity of supported oblique fragments without repeating the rejected threshold change.
